title: Cluster H — Yelets-Kursk family (P0775/P0776): duplicate REFUTED; ownership-attribution defect confirmed as its own concern

rows.recommendation: Do NOT merge or fold P0775 into P0776 — treat as a fully distinct, separately-sourced trunk line. Separately, have Update research the origin of the 'Gazprom PJSC [48.6%]' figure: it is the only non-round, non-100% Gazprom share among 19 comparable Russia-Ukraine cross-border gas rows in the current snapshot, all of which list Gazprom PJSC + Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine as co-owners with no defensible length- or asset-based derivation found for any of them. If no supporting document can be found for 48.6% specifically, flag the value as unsourced (do not fabricate a rationale) and consider whether GEM's cross-border ownership convention needs a documented rule. Also worth a look: both P0775 and P0776 carry the identical (and wrong) OtherLanguagePrimaryPipelineName 'Система газопроводов Уренгой - Помары - Ужгород' — that is a different, more famous corridor and looks like a copy-paste artifact, not a translation of either row's actual name.
rows.notes: DUPLICATE QUESTION: REFUTED. Two independent, non-GEM sources each name «Єлець—Курськ—Диканька» and «Єлець—Курськ—Київ» as separate 1220 mm trunk lines: (1) the Kursk Oblast district administration's official gas-corridor/security-zone listing (kurskr.rkursk.ru, archived 2022-05-19 at web.archive.org/web/20220519195206/http://kurskr.rkursk.ru/index.php?sub_menus_id=18020&id_mat=2996) states verbatim: '...Уренгой – Ужгород Ф1420мм, Елец – Курск – Диканька Ф1220мм, Елец – Курск – Киев Ф1220мм...' as two items in a corridor list, both 1220 mm — i.e. a Russian government body, independent of Gazprom, distinguishing them by name while giving them the SAME diameter, which rules out 'different diameter = different line, same diameter = the same line' as a shortcut; naming is what does the work here. (2) Gazprom Transgaz Moskva's own Kurskoe LPUMG page (moskva-tr.gazprom.ru/kurskoe-lpumg/, archived 2025-05-12) states in its historical-construction narrative: 'строятся магистральные газопроводы: «Елец — Курск — Киев», «Уренгой — Ужгород», «Елец — Курск — Диканька», «Елец — Кременчуг — Кривой Рог», магистральный газопровод «Прогресс»' — again both named as separate items in a list of distinct Soviet-era trunks built through the oblast. (3) uk.wikipedia's own dedicated article on «Єлець — Курськ — Диканька» (cites Kursk oblast admin, the Ukrtransgaz chronology, and two independent Lipetsk/Kursk regional gas-supply characterization documents) gives 1220 mm, 5.5 MPa, commissioned 1984 — matching GEM P0775's diameter and StartYear1 exactly. GEOMETRY (GEM's own drawn routes, corroborating from a fourth, independent-of-sourcing angle): P0775 and P0776 share only a 189.3 km Yelets-to-Kursk prefix, then physically diverge at Kursk (51.711, 36.157) — P0775 continues 239.0 km to Dykanka, P0776 continues 417.5 km to Kyiv, hundreds of km apart in different directions. That is the geometric signature of two lines sharing an origin/transit corridor, not one line recorded twice. CAPACITY (weaker, treat as single-origin, not independent corroboration): the live moskva-tr.gazprom.ru Kurskoe LPUMG page (fetched once successfully via curl with a browser UA on 2026-08-15; the site subsequently became intermittently unreachable to both direct fetch and archive.org's Save-Page-Now, which returned 523 origin-unreachable — this is a live-site availability problem, not a dead-link finding, and I could not get url_verifier.py to pass on the live URL for that reason) lists 'Елец-Курск-Диканька» диаметр трубы 1220 мм ... производительность 65 млн. м3/сут' and 'Елец-Курск-Киев» диаметр трубы 1220 мм ... производительность 45 млн. м3/сут'. 65 and 45 million m3/day annualize to 23.725 and 16.425 bcm/y — matching GEM's stated 23.73 and 16.43 bcm/y on P0775/P0776 almost to the decimal. That precision match is too exact to be coincidence, but it cuts the other way on independence: it suggests this same characteristics document (or a shared upstream) may be the actual origin of GEM's own capacity figures, so it should NOT be counted as a second independent source validating the capacity VALUES — only as further confirmation that the two lines are tracked as separate items with separate capacities. LENGTH: no source (this batch or the two Wikipedia/Gazprom/rkursk documents) gives an explicit km figure for either line, so the near-identical 298.00/297.00 km on the sheet remains UNSOURCED in both directions; the Ukrainian-territory-portion hypothesis from the brief is neither confirmed nor ruled out here (border-to-Dykanka is roughly 170 km and border-to-Kyiv roughly 380 km by my own rough estimate, neither close to ~297, but this was not independently sourced and should not be treated as a finding). MINOR SPEC NOTE: search snippets (not a dedicated article, so weaker/uncorroborated) give 1982 for the Kyiv line's commissioning vs GEM's StartYear1=1981 for P0776 — a one-year discrepancy worth a follow-up Update ref-sweep item, not a duplicate signal. ADJACENT CONTEXT (P0783, P1453): per route_geometry_findings.md's cluster-F test, P0783 (Yelets-Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rih, 1420 mm) does NOT geometrically concatenate from P0775+P1460 (0 of 3 P1460 vertices and only 1 of 3 P0775 vertices lie on P0783's trace), and the three rows carry three different diameters (1420/1220/700 mm) — the signature of distinct parallel pipes in a shared corridor, not a triple-count. That is cluster F's finding, not re-adjudicated here. P1453 (Yefremivka-Dykanka-Kyiv) is documented in kzu_evidence.md as part of the 1970 KZU-1 commissioning cohort, a third distinct line converging on the same Dykanka hub — consistent with Dykanka being a genuine multi-line junction, not evidence that any of these rows duplicate each other.

rows.recommendation: Do NOT merge or fold P0776 into P0775 — distinct, separately-sourced trunk line (see P0775 notes for the full duplicate-refutation evidence, which applies symmetrically to both rows). This row's ownership entry is the more clear-cut defect and should be prioritized: 'Gazprom PJSC [100.%]; Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' is internally contradictory — a 100% share for one listed co-owner leaves nothing for the second co-owner, and Gazprom is documented to own no Ukrainian pipeline section (standing project fact), yet this line's own row lists Ukraine as an end country and GTSOU as a co-owner. Recommend Update research whatever cross-border ownership convention GEM intends here (the '100.%' formatting — note the stray period — recurs on several other Russia-Ukraine rows like P0768 Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod and P2387 Shebelinka-Belgorod-Kursk-Bryansk, suggesting a default/boilerplate value rather than a researched split) and correct it to something internally consistent, e.g. a genuine Russia-side/Ukraine-side split mirroring how P0775 is structured, or remove the percentage entirely if no split can be sourced. This pattern recurs across at least seven other Russia-Ukraine cross-border gas rows in the current snapshot (P0761, P0768, P0793, P1471, P2387, and the unpercentaged P0774/P0779/P0783/P0788-P0791/P1455/P1457/P1465), so this may be a systemic data-entry convention problem worth a scope wider than this cluster — flagging for Update/QC to decide whether a tracker-wide review is warranted.
rows.notes: Same duplicate-refutation evidence as P0775 (two independent official sources — Kursk Oblast district administration's archived corridor list and Gazprom Transgaz Moskva's own archived Kurskoe LPUMG history page — each name this line separately from the Dykanka line; GEM's own route geometry shows the two rows diverging at Kursk toward destinations 417.5 km apart). OWNERSHIP is the sharper concern on this specific row: 'Gazprom PJSC [100.%]' directly contradicts the co-listed 'Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' (100% to one owner leaves 0% for the other, which is not what a two-owner entry normally means) and contradicts the project's own standing fact that Gazprom owns no Ukrainian pipeline section — yet this line terminates in Kyiv, Ukraine. I could not find any source (this batch's ladder) that assigns Gazprom a literal 100% share of this line; the figure appears to be an unfilled/default value rather than a researched one, especially set against P0775's row on the very same family carrying a distinct 48.6% figure with no clearer sourcing either. Checking the wider snapshot (data/GGIT_gas_snapshot_20260812.csv) shows the same 'Gazprom PJSC [100.%]' string appears verbatim on P0768 (Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod) and P2387 (Shebelinka-Belgorod-Kursk-Bryansk) — both of which also cross into Ukraine and also list no percentage for a Ukrainian co-owner (P2387 lists no Ukrainian owner at all despite CountriesOrAreas = 'Russia, Ukraine') — so '100.%' reads as a boilerplate/default rather than row-specific research. Also noted, low priority: this row shares GEM's identical (wrong) OtherLanguagePrimaryPipelineName with P0775 ('Система газопроводов Уренгой - Помары - Ужгород', a different pipeline entirely) — looks like a copy-paste metadata artifact, flagged for awareness, not adjudicated as part of the duplicate question. MINOR SPEC NOTE: unconfirmed search snippets suggest 1982 as this line's commissioning year vs GEM's StartYear1=1981 — a one-year gap from a source too weak (search snippet, not a dedicated citable article) to act on, logged as an open question for the next ref-sweep pass.

summary: GEM's P0775 (Yelets-Kursk-Dykanka, 298.00 km, 1220 mm, 23.73 bcm/y, 1984) and P0776 (Yelets-Kursk-Kyiv, 297.00 km, 1220 mm, 16.43 bcm/y, 1981) share an origin, a transit node, a diameter, and a length that differs by only 1 km -- a genuinely compelling structural signature for a duplicate. On sourcing, that hypothesis is REFUTED. Two sources independent of both Gazprom and GEM -- the Kursk Oblast district administration's own gas-corridor/security-zone listing, and (separately) Gazprom Transgaz Moskva's own Kurskoe LPUMG historical narrative -- each name 'Елец-Курск-Диканька' and 'Елец-Курск-Киев' as two distinct 1220 mm trunk lines built in the same construction wave through the oblast, before diverging toward different destinations. GEM's own route geometry independently corroborates this from a fourth angle: the two drawn routes share a 189.3 km Yelets-to-Kursk prefix, then physically split at Kursk, running 239.0 km to Dykanka (P0775) versus 417.5 km to Kyiv (P0776) -- destinations several hundred km apart, exactly matching what the two names claim. A uk.wikipedia article dedicated to the Dykanka line (citing Kursk oblast admin, the Ukrtransgaz chronology, and two regional gas-supply characterization documents) independently confirms its 1220 mm diameter and 1984 commissioning year against GEM's P0775 values. No source in this batch's ladder produced an explicit km figure for either line, so the near-identical 298.00/297.00 km remains an unexplained coincidence rather than a data-entry tell -- neither confirmed as an in-country-portion convention nor otherwise accounted for. A live fetch of the Gazprom page's capacity table gave 65 vs 45 million m3/day for the two lines, annualizing to 23.725/16.425 bcm/y -- matching GEM's capacities on both rows almost to the decimal. That precision is likely evidence the same document underlies GEM's own capacity figures rather than a fully independent corroboration of the numbers, but it still corroborates the naming distinctness; the site became intermittently unreachable immediately afterward (confirmed by archive.org's own crawler also getting a 523), so this specific citation could not be re-verified with url_verifier.py and is flagged as directly-observed-but-not-tool-verified rather than omitted. Ownership is a separate, real, and more clear-cut defect on both rows, reported regardless of the duplicate verdict per the brief: P0775 carries an anomalous 'Gazprom PJSC [48.6%]' with no discoverable derivation, and P0776 carries 'Gazprom PJSC [100.%]' alongside a co-listed Ukrainian operator -- an internal contradiction, since 100% to one owner leaves nothing for the other, and Gazprom is documented to own no Ukrainian pipeline section even though this line ends in Kyiv. Checking the wider GGIT gas snapshot shows this exact '100.%' string, and the broader pattern of unexplained or missing ownership splits on Russia-Ukraine cross-border rows, recurring on at least seven other rows -- suggesting a systemic default-value problem rather than a P0775/P0776-specific error, which I've flagged for Update/QC to scope more broadly. Adjacent context checked per the brief: cluster F's own geometry test already shows P0783 (1420 mm) does not geometrically concatenate from P0775+P1460 and the three rows carry three different diameters, so no triple-count; P1453 is documented as part of a separate 1970 KZU-era commissioning cohort converging on the same Dykanka hub, consistent with Dykanka being a genuine multi-line junction rather than evidence of duplication anywhere in this family.

P0776's commissioning year: GEM says 1981, unconfirmed search snippets say 1982 -- worth a dedicated ref-sweep search pass since no citable dedicated source was found either way in this ladder.
